title: Cost-aware quantile prefill/decode scheduler for tail-latency vs token-cost tradeoffs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement a tenant-aware, cost-aware prefill/decode scheduling policy that uses quantile-based utility functions to balance tail latency (e.g., 95th/99th percentile) against per-token cost. The scheduler should produce split/merge decisions for prefill+decode phases and emit kernel hints for downstream selection, enabling configurable tradeoffs for latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive tenants.
background: Current phase-splitting schedulers prioritize latency fairness across tenants and phases but lack explicit cost signals. Some tenants are highly cost-sensitive (e.g., embeddings-heavy workloads) while others are latency-critical. Existing work enumerated in our backlog optimizes phase splitting and kernel affinity for latency or throughput, but we need a mechanism that explicitly incorporates token-cost and tenant budget constraints into scheduling decisions so tenants can express utility for cost vs tail latency.
proposed_solution: Introduce a quantile-based utility model per tenant that combines scaled tail-latency penalty (configurable percentiles) and expected token-cost penalty. Scheduler computes per-request utility delta for different phase split strategies (e.g., merge prefill+decode vs split into microphases) and selects the action that maximizes aggregate utility under current capacity. Admission control allows low-utility, cheap requests to be delayed in favor of high-utility, latency-sensitive work. Kernel-selection hints are emitted with expected sequence-length/phase profile to improve kernel probe accuracy.
design_details:
1) Tenant configuration: new tenant preferences API accepts fields: latency_percentile (string, e.g., "p95"), latency_weight (0.0-1.0), cost_weight (0.0-1.0), budget_mode ("soft"|"hard") and quantile_thresholds (list of percentiles).
2) Utility function: U = -latency_weight * normalized_tail_latency(p) - cost_weight * normalized_expected_token_cost. Normalization uses historical baselines per model and region.
3) Scheduler flow: compute utility for candidate split actions using lightweight simulation (O(1) heuristics + cached kernel cost table), prioritize by descending marginal utility, enforce tenant budget soft/hard rules, and mark selected requests with split decisions and kernel_hints = [kernel_id, preferred_batch_shape, kv_cache_reuse_hint].
4) Quantile-based prioritization: maintain sliding-window estimates for p50/p95/p99 latency per tenant+model; use the selected percentile from tenant config when computing latency_penalty.
5) Cost estimation: per-token cost computed from model+precision+kernel table; reuse caching multipliers for prefix reuse.
6) Fallbacks: if kernel probing fails, fall back to latency-first policy with shorter microphase sizes.
7) Telemetry: emit decision_reason, estimated_utility, chosen_action, and baseline_metrics for offline analysis.
metrics:
Acceptance criteria: 
- p95 tail latency for latency_weight>=0.8 tenants does not regress by >5% compared to baseline when under normal load.
- Average token-cost reduction >=8% for cost_weight>=0.8 tenants across representative workloads.
- Overall scheduler decision latency <2ms added per request on median.
- Decision accuracy: kernel hinting leads to correct kernel selection (matching offline probe) >=90% of the time in A/B.
- Telemetry shows expected utility correlates with realized latency and cost (Spearman rho >0.6).
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind runtime-quantile-scheduler.
2) Canary: enable for internal infra tenants (10% traffic) for 2 weeks. Measure metrics above.
3) Expand to beta customers who opt-in via tenant prefs.
4) Gradual ramp to all tenants with cost_weight default 0.3 and latency_weight default 0.7.
5) Provide opt-out and emergency kill in Console.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for utility computation and normalization.
- Integration tests with kernel cost table mocks to validate split decisions.
- Load test scenarios: mixed-tenants synthetic workload (latency-sensitive + cost-sensitive) to validate throughput and scheduler CPU overhead.
- Shadow experiments for 2 weeks, compare decisions to baseline policy.
- A/B on real traffic for kernel hint correctness and customer-visible latency/cost impacts.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Miscalibrated normalization leads to poor utility tradeoffs. Mitigation: conservative defaults, offline calibration job, expose per-tenant baseline adjustments.
- Risk: Additional scheduler CPU latency at high QPS. Mitigation: keep decision heuristics O(1), cache cost computations, use vectorized batch evaluation.
- Risk: Kernel hint mismatch causing lower throughput. Mitigation: fast fallback to previous kernel selection; include kernel probe reconciliation metrics and auto-tune thresholds.
- Risk: Customers misconfigure weights harming their SLAs. Mitigation: provide safe presets ("latency-first", "balanced", "cost-first") and Console guidance with simulated impact before applying.
open_questions: How should we surface historical per-tenant baselines in the Console for normalization transparency?
What is an acceptable default for quantile_thresholds — p95 only or p95+p99?
Should budget_mode "hard" trigger immediate throttling at the ingress layer or graceful de-prioritization in the scheduler?
Can existing kernel cost tables be extended to include cache-hit multipliers per model variant?
notes: Related research: internal latency-vs-cost whitepaper (drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/latency-cost-whitepaper) — prototype simulations show 12% cost savings for cost-weighted workloads.
